On Monday morning, Nvidia's board of directors voted unanimously to
immediately reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board director.
Huang resigned less than two weeks ago, following reports that he had multiple
affairs, including with a
[suspected](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/politics/nvidia-china-
jensen-huang-trump.html) Chinese spy.

Donald Trump and other senior administration officials worked the phones in a
private pressure campaign to push Nvidia to give Huang his job back, per two
sources with knowledge of the matter.

A White House official tells **Zeteo** the U.S. president personally "made it
a priority," because he felt that strongly about it.

Nvidia, for its part, alluded to this pressure campaign in a press
[release](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-board-reinstates-jensen-
huang-as-president-ceo-and-board-director) announcing Huang's reinstatement:
"In the process of reaching its decision, the board received input from senior
levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the board is
confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk," the
company said.

Nvidia is the world's largest AI chip company, and one of the most valuable
companies on the planet. Trump himself is a [huge
investor](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/trump-nvidia-stock-trades-jensen-
huang.html) in the company; earlier this month, CNBC estimated that he held up
to $57.7 million worth of Nvidia stock.

Prior to Huang's reinstatement Nvidia's stock had been tanking, leading
[some](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/ai-bubble-finally-
popping-nvidia-140106035.html) observers to speculate the market's AI bubble
was on the brink of finally bursting.

Nvidia's stock shot up about $40 Monday morning from where it closed on
Friday.

On Monday morning, Trump spoke with CNN and
[predicted](https://x.com/ElizLanders/status/2124857975495860666?a=w936c69QdGYkyuucp90&s=20)
Nvidia would rehire Huang. He refused to comment on a
[report](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/22/us/politics/alice-huang-china-spy-
agency-nvidia.html?unlocked_article_code=1.SlE.HiO2.2vnWtUqkyP-O&smid=url-
share) from the _New York Times_ that found the woman Huang had an affair with
had been in contact with China's top spy agency. "I am not going to comment on
anything having to do with that," he said, before claiming: "He did absolutely
nothing wrong from that standpoint."

Speaking with CNBC, Trump
[said](https://x.com/BulwarkClips/status/2124885828581179774) Huang
"apologized for indiscretion, which was unfortunate. That was probably what
brought it to such a level, because sex sells."

The controversy around Nvidia first erupted following revelations that Huang
had been involved in an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who was suspected
by U.S. officials of being tied to Chinese intelligence. Huang
[acknowledged](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/a-message-to-our-company)
being unfaithful, and admitted he had fallen short of the responsibilities he
owed to the company and its shareholders.

[Share](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-nvidia-jensen-huang-job-
back?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&action=share)

The episode was followed by reports of two more alleged relationships Huang
had maintained with Nvidia employees. But it is Jensen Huang's relationship
with the Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, that has fueled much of the
controversy.

Alice Huang is a former senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data
center company and Nvidia business partner. U.S. intelligence
[suspects](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/22/us/politics/alice-huang-china-
spy-agency-nvidia.html) possible ties between Huang and Chinese intelligence.
The concern is that Alice Huang might have used the relationship with the
Nvidia CEO to gain access to sensitive information about Nvidia, amid the AI
race between the U.S. and China.

All the while, since last year, Singapore has been
[investigating](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jensen-huang-nvidia-alice-huang-
singapore-investigation-china-chips/) whether Alice Huang and Megaspeed had
worked to ship computer servers equipped with Nvidia chips to China.

Last week, the U.S.
[confirmed](https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/us-confirms-probing-
megaspeed-over-060823086.html) it too has been investigating Megaspeed since
2024 over whether it has been ultimately shipping Nvidia chips to Chinese
customers, in violation of export restrictions the U.S. has imposed to prevent
such transfers. Jay Clayton, director of national intelligence,
[acknowledged](https://abcnews.com/Politics/week-transcript-11-22-26-director-
national-intelligence/story?id=138345755) Sunday that "there is an
investigation ongoing into [Alice Huang's] firm and into her."

The stream of allegations has had even Republican members of Congress speaking
out. On the Megaspeed affair, Indiana Republican Senator Jim Banks
[told](https://www.banks.senate.gov/news/press-releases/icymi-sen-banks-joins-
america-reports-on-fox-news-channel-4/) Fox that "the Department of Commerce,
Secretary Lutnick, it appears, used loopholes to allow some of these chip
sales to occur even though President Trump has directed his administration and
the Department of Commerce not to allow that to happen."

Louisiana Republican Senator John Kennedy nearly accused Lutnick's department
of treason. "It appears to me, I emphasize _appears_ , that the Department of
Commerce has allowed the Communist Party of China to circumvent our export
controls on advanced chips," Kennedy
[said](https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/6236748-john-kennedy-howard-
lutnick-nvidia-probe-
questions/https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/6236748-john-kennedy-howard-
lutnick-nvidia-probe-questions/) on Sunday, adding: "It appears that they
knowingly allowed this to happen."

As Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang, it said it is still conducting a probe
through a "committee comprised solely of independent directors," citing
reports that the Nvidia CEO was "the target of a foreign intelligence effort."

"The board reiterated that the committee's investigation will proceed to
conclusion," the company [said](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-
board-reinstates-jensen-huang-as-president-ceo-and-board-director) Monday.
"Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating
with it."
